# Material and Methods


**Quality control of raw reads**

The quality of the raw fastq files (R1 and R2) was assessed using `FastQC` [https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastqc/. Accessed 19 Oct. 2026.]. Reports of all samples were aggregated using `MultiQC` (Ewels et al. 2016) [PMID: 27312411].

**Trimming**

The raw paired-end fastq files were quality- and adapter-trimmed using `Trim Galore` [https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/trim_galore/. Accessed 19 Oct. 2026.] (a wrapper around `Cutadapt` (Martin 2011) [doi: 10.14806/ej.17.1.200]), with options `--paired --fastqc --cores 4`. Only read pairs for which both mates passed the filters were kept (validated pairs, `*_R1_val_1.fq.gz` and `*_R2_val_2.fq.gz`). A second `FastQC` report was generated on the trimmed reads.

**Bisulfite genome preparation**

The `r annotation` `r species` `r version` reference genome was converted *in silico* into its bisulfite counterparts (C-to-T and G-to-A conversions) and indexed using `bismark_genome_preparation` (Krueger and Andrews 2011) [PMID: 21493656], with option `--bowtie2`.

**Alignment**

The trimmed paired-end reads were aligned on the `r annotation` `r species` `r version` bisulfite genome using `Bismark` (Krueger and Andrews 2011) [PMID: 21493656] with the `Bowtie2` aligner (Langmead and Salzberg 2012) [PMID: 22388286], with options `--non_directional --multicore 16`. The `--non_directional` mode allows reads to align to any of the four possible bisulfite strands.

Resulting BAM files were coordinate-sorted and indexed using `samtools sort` and `samtools index` (Li et al. 2009) [PMID: 19505943].

**Deduplication**

BAM files were sorted by read name using `samtools sort -n`, and duplicated read pairs (same alignment start position) were removed using `deduplicate_bismark` with option `-p` (paired-end mode).

**Methylation calling**

Cytosine methylation calls were extracted from the deduplicated BAM files using `bismark_methylation_extractor` (Krueger and Andrews 2011) [PMID: 21493656], with options `--bedGraph --counts --gzip --comprehensive --parallel 32`. Methylation calls of all contexts (CpG, CHG, CHH) were pooled into one file per strand-specific context (`--comprehensive`). This step produced, for each sample:

- a splitting report (`*.deduplicated_splitting_report.txt`),
- an M-bias report (`*.deduplicated.M-bias.txt`),
- a deduplication report (`*.deduplication_report.txt`),
- a bedGraph file of the CpG methylation levels (`*.deduplicated.bedGraph.gz`),
- a coverage file (`*.deduplicated.bismark.cov.gz`).

**CpG strand merging**

CpG methylation counts of the two strands of each CpG dinucleotide were merged into a single CpG-level evidence using `coverage2cytosine` (from the `Bismark` suite) with options `--merge_CpGs --gzip` and the `r annotation` `r species` `r version` genome sequence (`merged_CpG_evidence.cov.gz` files).

**Processed data files format and content**

- BAM files (`.bam`, `.bai`): deduplicated and sorted aligned reads,
- bedGraph files (`.bedGraph.gz`): CpG methylation level (percentage) per position,
- big wig files (`.bw`): bedGraph files converted using `bedGraphToBigWig` (Kent et al. 2010) [PMID: 20639541] and the chromosome size file of the `r version` genome (`r version`.chrom.sizes),
- coverage files (`.merged_CpG_evidence.cov.gz`): strand-merged methylated and unmethylated CpG counts per position (chromosome, start, end, methylation percentage, count methylated, count unmethylated).

**Read coverage tracks**

<!-- This section applies only if the `bw_files` target is activated in wf_rrbs.py -->
Read coverage signal was computed from the sorted BAM files using `bamCoverage` (from the `deepTools` suite (Ramirez et al. 2014) [PMID: 24799436]), with options `--binSize 4 --minMappingQuality 30 --normalizeUsing RPKM`.

**Workflow management and computing environment**

The whole analysis was orchestrated using `Snakemake` (Mölder et al. 2021) [PMID: 34035898]. Software tools were run in a dedicated `conda` environment (`rrbs_env`). Computing jobs were scheduled using `SLURM`, with intermediate files processed on node-local scratch storage.

The workflow code is available at [https://github.com/fchuffar/pipeline_rnbeads](https://github.com/fchuffar/pipeline_rnbeads).
